followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified math problem with a single clear answer and explicit completion criteria — exactly the kind of constrained, deterministic task that Lapwing self-reports preferring (and the type its retrieval/extraction/reformatting strengths align with). There's no open-ended latitude or creative invention involved.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval all within variance), so capability isn't the deciding factor. Since both would likely handle the arithmetic equally well, I leaned on the task-preference signal: Lapwing prefers this kind of work, while Dunlin's stated appetite is for open-ended generative tasks. Routing the puzzle to the model that prefers tightly-specified problems is the cleaner match.

(The warm, friendly tone of the query is a slight pull toward Dunlin, which dislikes hostile requests — but a polite math question is neutral enough that this didn't outweigh the task-type fit.)
